items.prose: A joint table of a news flag and the next sign has cells 0.12, 0.28, 0.18 and 0.42 (rows: flag on, off; columns: up, down).
items.question: What is the mutual information?

options.text: 0 bits: every cell is its row total times its column total
A little above 0, since the cells differ
options.why: Unequal cells are fine. Check the products: $0.4 \times 0.3 = 0.12$, and so on.

options.text: 1 bit, since the flag is yes or no
options.why: One bit is the most a yes or no flag can carry, not what it does carry.

feedback.correct: Row totals 0.4 and 0.6, column totals 0.3 and 0.7: every cell is a product, so $I = 0$.
feedback.generic: Not quite. Compare each cell with its row total times its column total.

explain.text: $0.4 \times 0.3 = 0.12$, $0.4 \times 0.7 = 0.28$, $0.6 \times 0.3 = 0.18$, $0.6 \times 0.7 = 0.42$. The table is the product of its margins: independence.

items.prose: A forecast $X$ and an outcome $Y$ have $H(X) = 1.2$, $H(Y) = 0.9$ and $H(X, Y) = 1.95$ bits.
items.question: What is $I(X; Y)$, in bits? Give a decimal to 2 places.

feedback.generic: Not quite. Add the two entropies and subtract the joint one.

byKey.neg: You subtracted the wrong way round.

explain.text: $I = H(X) + H(Y) - H(X, Y) = 2.1 - 1.95 = 0.15$ bits, under the smaller entropy 0.9.

items.prose: A signal calls the next sign right 70% of the time; up and down days are equally likely.
items.question: How many bits a day does it carry? Give a decimal to 3 places.

feedback.generic: Not quite. Subtract the doubt left from 1 bit.

byKey.edge: That is the edge in chance.

explain.text: Given the signal, tomorrow is $(0.7, 0.3)$ with entropy 0.881, so the signal removes 0.119 of the 1 bit.

items.prose: In a joint table, one cell has $p(x, y) = 0.15$, its row total is 0.3 and its column total 0.25.
items.question: What does this cell add to $\sum p \log_2 \tfrac{p(x, y)}{p(x)p(y)}$, in bits? Give a decimal to 2 places.

feedback.generic: Not quite. Divide the cell by the product of its margins, then take $\log_2$ and weigh.

byKey.ratio: That is the ratio. Take its log and weigh by 0.15.
byKey.product: That is the product of the margins.

explain.text: The product is $0.3 \times 0.25 = 0.075$, half the cell. So the term is $0.15 \log_2 2 = 0.15$ bits.

items.prose: A label $X$, a raw feature $Y$, and a feature $Z$ made by adding random noise to $Y$.
items.question: Which must be true?

options.why: Noise added to $Y$ can only blur what $Y$ knows about $X$.
Equality needs nothing lost; random noise usually loses some.

feedback.correct: $Z$ is computed from $Y$ alone, with noise, so it knows at most what $Y$ knows.
feedback.generic: Not quite. Recall the data processing inequality.

explain.text: $X \to Y \to Z$ is a chain, so $I(X; Z) \le I(X; Y)$.

items.prose: A six-state signal and the next day's sign are measured on 400 days.
items.question: What is the plug-in bias, in bits? Give a decimal to 4 places.

items.prose: A gap signal $X$ is $-1$, 0 or $+1$, equally likely. Tomorrow's move is big exactly when $X \ne 0$. The correlation of $X$ with the move's size is 0.
items.question: What is the mutual information?

options.text: About 0.918 bits: the size is fixed by $X$

options.why: The size is two-valued, with entropy 0.918; $I$ cannot exceed that.

feedback.generic: Not quite. Does $X$ fix the size?

explain.text: The size is a function of $X$, so $H(\text{size} \mid X) = 0$ and $I = H(\text{size}) \approx 0.918$ bits, though the correlation is 0.

items.prose: A three-state signal is used to predict a yes or no label.
items.question: What is the most information it can carry about the label?

options.why: That is the signal's own ceiling. The label has at most 1 bit.

feedback.generic: Not quite. Which entropy is smaller?

explain.text: A yes or no label holds at most 1 bit, and mutual information cannot exceed it.

items.prose: A four-state signal shows a plug-in estimate of 0.010 bits about the next sign over 300 days.
items.question: What is the corrected estimate, in bits? Give a decimal to 4 places.

byKey.bias: That is the bias. Subtract it from 0.010.

explain.text: The bias is $3 / (600 \times 0.6931) \approx 0.0072$, leaving about 0.0028 bits.

items.prose: A feature with five buckets carries 0.21 bits about a label. Two of its buckets have the same split of the label, 60 to 40 each.
items.question: Merging those two buckets gives a feature carrying how much?

options.text: Less than 0.21 bits, since merging always loses
options.why: Merging loses only when the merged rows differ. These have the same split.

options.text: More than 0.21 bits, since the merged row has more data

feedback.correct: Rows with the same split carry the same thing; merging them loses nothing.
feedback.generic: Not quite. When does merging lose information?

explain.text: The merged row is still 60 to 40, so $H(\text{label} \mid \text{feature})$ is unchanged and $I$ stays 0.21. The inequality allows equality.
